text: I’m using the code-review skill for a read-only pass over only the named story files. I’ll check the current revision, scientific claims, animation state transitions, and focused geometry tests, then return evidence with exact lines and clear severity.

The first concrete issue is in the 3D handoff: the fourth-satellite scene keeps the two fixed candidates computed from the first three spheres even while all radii are being clock-corrected. I’m quantifying that mismatch and checking whether the error-triangle marker and Doppler vector match the equations they display.

The files changed during my pass, and several issues I was checking have already been addressed in the live source: clock correction now eases in, the fourth-sphere scene hides the invalid second candidate, and the Doppler note now states the clock-drift assumption. I’m re-reviewing the new hashes so the final findings don’t cite superseded code.

Reviewed snapshot: workspace base `245e5429a14be04df3d37e1930b807a7149bae1e`; all-new ignored project files, with final relevant hashes `main.js C061CC6E…`, `sketch.js ADCB495B…`, `space.js D824DDF3…`, `geometry.js ADFEB23C…`, `story.js 42587CA2…`, and `geometry.test.js 7EF1D91A…`.

Confirmed findings:

1. **Medium — Doppler’s drawn vectors disagree with the calculation on curved road segments.**  
   Trigger: any point where the car has nonzero vertical velocity. [sketch.js:74]([local-path]) computes `vx` and `vy`, and lines 75–76 correctly use both for the frequency animation. Lines 77–78 draw `v` horizontally and derive the sightline projection from `vx` alone. At local chapter time ≈8 s, the actual projection is about `−57.3` scene-units/s while the arrow represents `−37.8`, a 34% discrepancy.  
   Consequence: the wave compression and “nærmere/høyere frekvens” label can be mathematically correct while the arrows purporting to explain them show a different velocity.  
   Fix: draw the full tangent velocity `(vx, vy)`, define one consistent receiver-to-satellite unit vector using the same receiver point as the wave, and project with `u·v`. Derive `ṙ = u·(v_s−v)` from that same value.

2. **Medium — the reflected signal passes through the blocking building briefly after occlusion begins.**  
   Trigger: car x-position approximately `394.7–431.7`. The direct-ray intersection logic at [sketch.js:93]([local-path]) correctly detects entry into the shadow. The mirror construction at line 108 is also correct, but line 109 draws both reflected legs immediately for every `blocked` position without checking the return leg against the blocker. At `p.x=410`, the glass-to-car ray crosses the building’s right edge at `y≈408.8`, inside its `255–415` vertical extent; it does not clear the building bottom until `p.x≈431.7`.  
   Consequence: for roughly the first 37 pixels of the blocked region, the illustration shows a physically impossible echo path through the same building that blocks the direct signal.  
   Fix: test both reflected segments against the blocking rectangle. Show signal loss during the short transition, then reveal the echo only once source→glass and glass→receiver are both unobstructed. Gate the path and packets as well as the ghost car.

3. **Low — Next rewinds at the end instead of remaining at the endpoint.**  
   [main.js:25]([local-path]) clamps an out-of-range chapter index to the last chapter and seeks its start; [main.js:51]([local-path]) always calls it with `currentIndex+1`. In the outro, including at `5:45`, Next therefore jumps backward 13 seconds. The Play button’s endpoint replay behavior is otherwise correct.  
   Fix: disable Next in the final chapter, make it a no-op, or seek to `duration`; preserve Play as the explicit full-story replay control.

4. **Low — 3D intersection tubes are briefly stale during clock correction.**  
   [space.js:9]([local-path]) precomputes intersection circles from the uncorrected radii. Lines 38–40 inflate the rendered spheres while fading those fixed tubes in before correction reaches zero. At `t=9`, the tubes are at 50% opacity while every sphere still carries about `0.0133` units of common radius correction.  
   Consequence: a highlighted curve can sit slightly off the two surfaces it claims to intersect during the transition.  
   Fix: rebuild the curves for the current radii, or keep them hidden until the correction reaches zero.

The Doppler sign convention itself is coherent: with `u` from receiver to satellite, `ṙ = u·(v_s−v)` and `Δf ≈ −(f₀/c)ṙ` correctly map decreasing range to increased received frequency. The new clock-drift qualification is appropriate.

The three-sphere candidates satisfy all three distances; the fourth radius passes through the intended receiver and misses the second candidate by about `0.075` scene units. The updated fourth-sphere marker timing now avoids claiming that the rejected point is a four-sphere solution. Receiver clock bias is consistently treated as one common additive pseudorange term. The error scene now marks an actual least-squares fit rather than the triangle centroid.

Validation: `node --test tests/geometry.test.js` passed all 6 tests. The suite now covers least squares, circle/sphere intersections, and deterministic car motion. It does not yet encode the reflected-path visibility, Doppler vector consistency, sphere-transition intersections, or final-chapter Next behavior.

Scope was limited to `USER_PROMPTS.md`, `index.html`, `src/{main,story,sketch,space,geometry}.js`, `src/style.css`, and `tests/geometry.test.js`. I did not inspect any other variant and made no edits, commits, publication changes, or network calls.

I’ll recheck only the four fixes and their regression coverage against the current content hashes. I’ll avoid the rest of the project and return a resolved/unresolved acceptance result with exact lines.

All four findings are resolved in the reviewed snapshot.

- **Doppler vectors: resolved.** [geometry.js:23]([local-path]) defines one receiver-to-satellite unit vector and returns both the receiver projection and relative range rate. [sketch.js:73]([local-path]) uses the same receiver anchor for the wave and calculation; lines 74–79 include both `vx` and `vy` in the tangent velocity arrow, sightline projection, range-rate sign, and frequency animation. The regression test at [geometry.test.js:32]([local-path]) confirms vertical motion contributes and that the analytical range rate agrees with a finite-difference change in range.

- **Reflected-path obstruction: resolved.** [geometry.js:32]([local-path]) implements closed segment/rectangle intersection. [sketch.js:99]([local-path]) uses it for the direct ray and both reflected legs. Lines 110–116 gate the reflected lines, packets, detour claim, and ghost position on `echoVisible`; the transition now explicitly shows a brief loss of both direct and reflected signal. The regression test at [geometry.test.js:45]([local-path]) covers clear direct reception, the no-signal transition, a valid echo, and restored direct sight.

- **Final-chapter Next behavior: resolved.** [main.js:28]([local-path]) disables Next whenever the final chapter is active. A disabled button does not dispatch its click handler, so the clamped `jump()` helper can no longer rewind the outro through this control. The full-story replay remains on Play at the endpoint.

- **Stale 3D intersection tubes: resolved.** [space.js:40]([local-path]) waits until the incoming sphere reaches full radius at 3.2 seconds before revealing its intersections. In the fourth-sphere chapter, the additional multiplier keeps every tube invisible until 10 seconds, when the common radius correction in line 38 is exactly zero. The receiver marker follows the same timing at line 41.

`node --test tests/geometry.test.js` passed all **8/8** tests. I found no remaining scientific or interaction consequence in these four fixes. Browser confirmation of the disabled Next control was outside this focused source recheck and is already covered by the parent’s running browser suite.

I’ll verify only the return-route equations, their out/back regression test, removal of the Doppler motion caption, and the two camera framing constants.

Accepted. No defect found in the narrow follow-up.

- [geometry.js:216]([local-path]) now uses the correct return derivative, `−55π cos(πp) p′`, and line 217 uses `425 − 55 sin(πp)`. The car therefore retraces the outbound road with continuous position and speed.
- [geometry.test.js:45]([local-path]) compares symmetric outbound/return coordinates and independently checks the road equation.
- [sketch.js:70]([local-path]) limits the moving/stopped caption to the position-velocity chapter, removing it from Doppler.
- [space.js:37]([local-path]) widens the camera to `26.8`, raises it to `5.2`, and aims at `y=1.1`, matching the intended framing adjustment.

`node --test tests/geometry.test.js` passed **9/9** tests. Camera clipping remains a visual acceptance matter, but the requested source change is present and consistent.
